slides.title:
Spatial organization and age-prediction value
of cortical column profiles
slides.notes: Advisor discussion deck. All results are from the latest saved formal Figure 4 and LSQR Figure 5 outputs. These analyses describe spatial profile organization and prediction under a fixed model; they do not establish independent biological units or a unique optimal scale.

slides.title: Two linked questions guide the analysis
Cohort definition: 320 spatial profiles, 196 CN prediction participants
slides.notes: Metadata: 448; imaging available: 369; complete profiles: 325; remove five visually confirmed registration failures: 320; date eligible: 268; CN: 200; ≥95% coverage: 196. Original and updated cohort files are preserved separately. Counts are sequential, not independent exclusions.

slides.title: Sample composition and age coverage
slides.notes: Diagnosis labels are harmonized at the QIAL-matched clinical visit; ambiguous/LOW matches occur in Figure 4. Age is VISIT_AGE at that visit, not an independently verified scan-date age. Sex codes remain numeric because their codebook was not verified; no male/female interpretation is assumed.
slides.source: Source: cohort_manifest.csv joined to the Figure 4 and final Figure 5 subject lists.

slides.title: From full fsaverage to the analyzed column representations
slides.notes: Full fsaverage has 163,842 vertices per hemisphere (327,684 bilateral). Reference in_analysis_mask has 149,953 left +149,926 right =299,879 positions. This is a fixed template analysis-mask count, not the valid count for every participant. Subject-specific validity varies. The masks retain 1,175/4,687/18,742 ico3/4/5 centers, pooled across hemispheres. Official ico mesh totals before mask: 1,284/5,124/20,484. Depth fractions are 0, .05, ..., 1, directed pial to white.
slides.source: Sources: build_features.py; feature_build_report.json; reference profile masks; spacing summary.

slides.title: Figure 4 methods: distance-dependent profile differences
slides.notes: Pair list contains 4,182,592 directed pairs across bins. K=15 is a target maximum per anchor-bin; sparse bins can contain fewer candidates. Self pairs and duplicates are excluded. Distances are mesh-edge geodesics on fsaverage white. Aggregation for A: pair metric → anchor × 2-mm-bin median → bilateral subject median → group median/IQR. Mean profile shape is preserved in raw r, so high far-distance r does not indicate independent profiles.
slides.source: Sources: formal notebook; formal_pair_qc.json; Figure 4A group tables.

slides.title: Figure 4A: nearby columns are more similar
slides.notes: Native PowerPoint line segments reproduce the saved median and IQR curves. IQR describes between-participant dispersion, not the confidence interval of the median. The reference plateau is 20–30 mm; it is an approximate reference, not a claim of perfect flatness.

slides.title: Figure 4A: correlated profiles still differ in MD magnitude
slides.notes: Symmetric relative MAE is normalized by the sum of the two median absolute MD values. It is not the conventional per-depth MAPE and should not be described as such. Shape and magnitude metrics answer different questions.

slides.title: Figure 4B: acquisition and sampling explain part of local similarity
slides.notes: Generate independent Gaussian noise on each native DWI grid, sample at real O3 coordinates with trilinear interpolation, then recolor to match subject-specific depth mean and 21×21 covariance. FWHM=0 means no additional Gaussian PSF, not an absence of interpolation-induced smoothness. Local excess L(d)=D_far−D(d), far reference 20–30 mm. Residual=L_real−L_null. AUC is not a proportion of biological information. Nonzero PSF sensitivity from older analyses is not merged into this formal primary result.
slides.source: Sources: formal Figure 4B notebook and seed-fixed acquisition-null cohort tables.

slides.title: Figure 4C: a stable millimeter-scale summary of spatial similarity
slides.notes: λ is the e-folding length of fitted excess similarity, not a hard radius of independence. Fixed anchor split is stratified by hemisphere × DK region and reused across all bins. This is anchor split-half stability, not scan-rescan reliability. Full data: all 320 fits acceptable. Half fits: 320 paired acceptable; no retained fit hits a parameter boundary. Acceptance: R² ≥ .5 and no boundary hit.

slides.title: Figure 4D: no consistent positive DK-boundary shape effect
slides.notes: ΔD=(1−r_across)−(1−r_within). Aggregate matched-pair mean → anchor-bin mean → bilateral subject-region-bin mean → equal-region subject-bin mean → group median/IQR. Effect is conditional on boundary-eligible anchors and distance matching. Curve uses varying eligible anchors across bins. It is not directly comparable to A’s all-anchor within-region medians. Earlier positive-boundary conclusions are superseded. A small negative aggregate does not establish that DK anatomy is invalid or that cross-region profiles are intrinsically more alike.
slides.source: Sources: formal boundary_matched cohort group and 0–10-mm summary tables.

slides.title: Figure 5 methods: a controlled representation comparison
slides.notes: Outer 5-fold CV, inner 5-fold CV, stratified by age quantile bins. Median imputation and StandardScaler fit within each training fold. Tune Ridge alpha over logspace(−4,6,21) using inner MAE; evaluate held-out outer folds. Metrics are recomputed from merged OOF predictions. Subject-bootstrap intervals condition on the saved OOF predictions; they do not include model retraining or resampling of the full CV pipeline. Age is from the matched clinical visit. Use fixed LSQR outputs consistently.
slides.source: Sources: run_ridge.py; saved fold definitions; submission_lsqr_20261028.json.

slides.title: Feature comparisons separate depth, spatial density, and geometry
slides.notes: Mean MD collapses depth within each column; regional mean MD also averages spatially within each DK region. Full ico4 depth features: 4,687×21=98,427. Adding length or curvature adds one scalar per center, 4,687 features each. Length is trajectory length; it is not automatically identical to cortical thickness. Native curvature is mapped using stored barycentric weights.
slides.source: Sources: feature_build_report.json; column-mean and geometry build reports.

slides.title: Depth profiles improve prediction over DK mean MD
slides.notes: Original seven-test comparison family: regional_mean_md−regional_profile ΔMAE=.442738, 95% CI [.149596,.739245], p=.002600, BH q=.018198. These are the original correction-family statistics, not the redefined family in the newer exploratory table.

slides.title: Spatial density: ico4 improves numerically; ico5 adds no observed gain
slides.notes: DK profile−ico4 ΔMAE=.347735; original bootstrap CI [.057035,.652521], unadjusted p=.019798; original seven-test BH q=.052728. ico4−ico5 ΔMAE=−.072997; CI [−.177822,.029289], q=.226777. A CI excluding zero combined with q>.05 is possible because CI is unadjusted and q is multiplicity adjusted. No equivalence or noninferiority claim is made.

slides.title: At ico4, depth and geometry yield modest additional changes
slides.notes: Column mean vs full depth added after reviewing results: exploratory unadjusted p=.161984, ΔMAE=.149993, CI [−.057946,.364215]. Full depth vs +length ΔMAE=.057147, CI [−.000321,.115386], original three-test geometry q=.160784. Curvature and combined geometry do not show supported additional improvements. Lowest numerical MAE should not be called statistically best.
slides.source: Sources: latest Figure 5 metrics and displayed paired statistics.

slides.title: Integrating spatial similarity with sampling density
slides.notes: Nearest-neighbor distances are pooled over retained template centers in both hemispheres, not over participants. Bands in the table are spatial IQRs. All use fsaverage white mesh-edge geodesics. Vertical lines show median center spacing on the Figure 4A curve; they do not represent a direct mapping of λ onto the prediction curve. λ is e-folding of profile excess similarity, not a theoretical optimum. No ico3-vs-ico4 significance is asserted here.
slides.source: Sources: formal Figure 4A/C; ico_nearest_neighbor_summary.csv; Figure 5 OOF metrics.

slides.title: Interpretation and questions for discussion
slides.notes: Suggested advisor discussion: whether to prioritize ico4 as a pragmatic working representation, whether the formal DK-boundary result merits a main or supplementary panel, and whether further validation should focus on repeated CV/external generalization rather than additional model ranking. Do not present planned analyses as completed.

slides.title: Appendix | Statistical contrasts and correction families
slides.notes: Δ is MAE(A)−MAE(B); positive favors B. Intervals are pointwise unadjusted percentile 95% intervals. Existing formal contrasts retain original multiplicity families: seven representation tests and three ico4 geometry tests. Column mean versus depth is exploratory and receives no q value. Fixed-OOF bootstrap does not quantify all training-set/CV variability.
